trans-unit.target: "Categories" groups the products. A category only appears in the shop from the moment it holds at least one product.
Introduce the category in a few lines: they are shown above the products, and read by the search engines.
It stays hidden for now: an empty category is not shown in the shop, it will appear as soon as it holds a product.
Give it a name: it is what the visitor reads in the shop's menu and at the top of the category page.
Add a category. The button opens an empty form; nothing is saved before the end of it.
The panel takes you to the categories: the list of every one of the shop, in the order it displays them.
Decide where it comes: the categories are sorted by ascending position, then by name.
Save. You come back to the list, where the new category is waiting for its first product.
Check the address. Filled in from the name, it is part of the public url: changing it later breaks the links already shared.
Here is what the buyer receives: an e-mail in the language the order was placed in, carrying links that expire. The customer area hands out those same copies, never a fresh one.
Edit the product. Any of them can sell a file, including one that also ships a parcel.
Attach the file in the item's own field. None of it is ever served straight from a public url.
Move down to the items: the file is carried by an item, not by the product. Two items can sell two different files.
The file is attached to an item, so we start from the product holding it: the panel takes you to the products.
Save: the file is stored out of the web server's reach, where only a paid order can read it.
The other site's import screen takes the archive as it is. The export group next to it dumps the raw table instead, which no import reads back.
The export works on a selection, so we start from the listing: the panel takes you to the products.
Export the selection: an archive is downloaded, holding the products, their pictures, their items and the files those are bought for.
Check what leaves: the header box takes the whole page, a narrower selection is checked row by row.
Edit the product selling the card, whether it was just created or has been in the catalog for a while.
The code is minted at the sale. Nothing more to do here: the card is issued once the order is paid, and the payment bundle is where it is read afterwards.
A gift card is created like any other product: the panel takes you to the same listing.
Save: the sheet is now selling a card rather than a parcel.
Hide the code: the scratch layer covers it until whoever receives the card rubs it off.
Write what is printed on it: the line the card carries beside its amount, a wish, a shop name, a season.
Set what it is worth. The amount lives on the item, next to its price: a card can be sold for less than it is worth.
Compose what stands above the listing. Delivery, arguments, a welcome message: the same kinds a page of the site is composed with.
Write the welcome line. It is the shop's own sentence, printed above everything else; left empty, the page falls back to the one the menu describes the shop with.
Open the shop page, in the left-hand menu. It is one screen for one row, and it opens straight on its form.
Save. The shop's index shows the line and the blocks as soon as the row is saved.
Say who it is for. Write the age as a range of figures, three dash eight, or fifteen dash from fifteen up: the sheet warns the visitor with it, and search engines read the audience off it.
Say when it becomes available. That is the date the shop states, on the sheet and in the structured data the search engines read.
Classify it. A product can belong to several categories, and it shows up under each of them.
Show it by unticking hidden: a hidden product stays visible here and nowhere else.
Add the first item: a product with no item has no price, and no way into the basket.
Move down to the items. The product says what it is; its items say what is bought, at what price, in which condition. The weight of each item is what the shipping cost is computed on.
Add a product. One single form holds the sheet, its media, its prices and the blocks around them.
The panel takes you to the products: the catalog as the shop reads it, trashed products excluded.
Fill in its price, its VAT rate and its currency, then its weight, which the parcel is charged on. The struck-through price is only filled if it really was charged over the last thirty days.
Save: the sheet is online the moment it is saved not hidden.
Give it a title: it is what the visitor reads first, and what the address is built from.
The visitor then sees a banner on every page of the shop, saying it is being set up. The payments have a test mode of their own, and the two are separate.
Turn it back off with the same button, the day the catalog is ready to be read as it stands.
Turn the test mode on: one click, no confirmation, and the shop is in it from the next page load.
The panel brings you back to the dashboard: the shortcut sits among the others, above the sections.
"Products" holds the catalog. The shop displays them by ascending position, then by title.
"Shop" opens the shop as a visitor reads it, in a new tab.
"Shop page" is what the shop says above the categories and the products it lists, composed with the same blocks as a product sheet.
